newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close up 1.44 pct on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close up 1.44 pct on fund buying.

text.p: Thai stocks on Wednesday ended a nine day declining streak with the index rising 1.44 percent after a private rescue fund entered the market and bought blue chip shares, brokers said.
"The key index could have fallen again today without buying from the rescue fund," said a local broker.

The SET index, which broke through the key psychological 1,000-point level around midday to hit an intra-day high of 1.001.12 points, retreated slightly later and ended up 14.13 points at 996.16. The SET-50 index gained 1.39 point to 75.83.
Part of the 15.7 billion baht rescue fund, contributed by commercial banks and brokerages, entered the market today and helped boost the market, brokers said.

"The index retreated slightly during the late afternoon session after foreigners sold stocks, especially energy issues, and took profits as they didn't have enough confidence in Thai politics," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.

Foreigners continued to sell stocks as debate on a no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa is due to begin in parliament next Wednesday. Net selling by foreigners on Tuesday amounted about 900 million baht.

Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, falling two baht to 161. Advanced Info Service rose six to 304. In the energy sector, Banpu slipped 26 to 590 and PTT Exploration and Production fell four to 322.
"The index is expected to rise, but only slightly, on Thursday due to continued buying by the private rescue fund," said Thaneit Khantigaroon of Ekachart Finance and Securities.
Support is seen around 980 points and resistance at 1,000 on Thursday, brokers said.
